family.tagline: A press and a bookshop, with the manuscripts kept close.
family.story: Odile writes and publishes; Seun edits and runs the shop. They keep a small independent press and bookshop on the ground floor of a brick farmhouse, with three children upstairs. Their manuscripts live on one Companion Core in the Library.

companion.name: Marguerite
companion.job: Drafts newsletter copy and catalog notes from what Odile texts it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Odile sends every word.

companion.name: Ike
companion.job: Opens Akaunting in its own browser and enters the day's shop sales.
companion.limits: Enters what Seun reads out. He checks the entry.

popup.title: The long way to the library
popup.body: A parcel waits under the white-columned porch. Seun carries it through the entry hall, the chess hall and the living room to the desk in the Library.

popup.title: Jules lines up the contents
popup.body: Jules lines up the contents: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The Core covers about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plugged in, among the manuscripts
popup.body: Odile plugs in the power cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Amara has the quickest thumbs
popup.body: Amara joins the Core's own Wi-Fi from her phone, then picks the home network and types its password.

popup.title: Agents and apps for a press
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Odile picks Hermes and Seun picks OpenClaw. They add Collabora Online, Listmonk and Akaunting, plus Companion Memory (beta). Then they walk away.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Marguerite says hello
popup.body: Odile sends her first message. Marguerite, the agent she named, answers.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: odile
say.text: Hello, Odile. I am Marguerite. Where does the story begin?

beats.capability: Stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Film night, adaptations first
popup.body: Seun picks a film made from a book. Jellyfin plays it on the living-room TV, and the family argues about the ending.

beats.capability: Read ebooks in your browser, with notes, highlights and text-to-speech

popup.title: A novel and its margins
popup.body: Amara reads a novel in Koodo Reader on the couch. Her notes and highlights sit on the Core, beside the press's ebooks.

beats.capability: Track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes

popup.title: A recipe, written down once
popup.body: Seun types his mother's soup recipe into Grocy at the breakfast bar. Now it sits beside the pantry list and the shopping list.

beats.capability: Team chat with channels, threads and files that stays on your Core

popup.title: Supper at seven, posted once
popup.body: Odile posts the supper time in a Mattermost channel. It reaches the shop floor and the Library over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: Edit documents, spreadsheets and presentations together in the browser

popup.title: Two editors, one page
popup.body: Odile drafts a chapter in Collabora Online. Seun edits the same page from the other end of the Library.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Marguerite drafts the newsletter
popup.body: Odile texts Marguerite the notes for the spring list. Marguerite drafts the newsletter from context in Companion Memory. Odile reads every word, then sends it from Listmonk.

say.speaker: odile
say.text: Draft ready. Please read every word.

beats.capability: Write a wiki or a set of manuals in books, chapters and pages, with search and history

popup.title: House style, with a history
popup.body: Seun writes the press house style in BookStack, as books, chapters and pages. Page history keeps every revision of every rule.

beats.capability: Edit audio in a browser tab

popup.title: A reading, cut and tidied
popup.body: Odile trims a poet's reading in AudioMass, in one browser tab. She cuts, fades and normalizes, and the file stays on the Core.

beats.capability: A whiteboard with a hand-drawn look

popup.title: Cover ideas, sketched together
popup.body: Seun sketches next season's cover ideas on an Excalidraw whiteboard. Odile adds her notes from the next desk.

beats.capability: Your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: Where the manuscripts live
popup.body: Unpublished manuscripts sit in one Nextcloud folder on the Core. They sync to Odile's laptop and to Seun's.

beats.capability: Invoicing, expenses, customers and profit and loss for a small business

popup.title: Ike enters the day's sales
popup.body: At closing, Seun reads out the day's shop sales. Ike enters them in Akaunting, in its own browser. Seun checks the totals.

say.speaker: seun
say.text: Sales entered. Please check the totals.

beats.capability: Turn a database into a spreadsheet-style app without writing code

popup.title: The stock list, after each delivery
popup.body: Seun updates the shop's stock list in NocoDB after each delivery. It works like a spreadsheet, and it runs on the Core.

beats.capability: A shared whiteboard on an infinite canvas

popup.title: A picture book, page by page
popup.body: Jules draws a picture book on a tldraw whiteboard, one page at a time. Odile adds the words, and the whole book stays on the Core.

beats.capability: Stream your own music from your Core to a browser or an app

popup.title: A lullaby, from the Core
popup.body: At bedtime, Odile plays the lullaby playlist from mStream in the baby's room. It streams from the Core.

beats.capability: Save articles to read later without a hosted bookmarking service

popup.title: From the telescope to Readeck
popup.body: Amara and Seun find Jupiter through the telescope. Then Amara saves an article about its moons in Readeck, to read later.

beats.capability: Capture quick notes and journal entries in Markdown

popup.title: Proof notes on the back porch
popup.body: On the back porch, Odile jots margin notes for the corrected proofs in Memos. They sit on the Core, ready for Monday's edit.

beats.capability: Control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: Garden lights for reading evenings
popup.body: Before the summer reading evening, Seun sets the garden lights in Home Assistant. They come on at dusk, run by the Core.

popup.title: A press, a shop, one Core
popup.body: A press, a bookshop and a family of five. The Lacroix-Adebayo household keeps every manuscript on one Companion Core.

closing.body: Keep your drafts, your paperwork and your mailing list on a Companion Core at home. A manuscript cannot be made twice, so keep it close.

notes: FTUE follows the owner-specified hotspot flow; the fact sheet says only "plug it in, pair it over Wi-Fi, and walk away". Owner sign-off open.
The house has no crib in its spec, so no beat says crib or nursery: the baby appears in "the baby's room". Jules is never given a pronoun. Children are never voiced.
Public shop, online orders and card payments are held (remote access), so the shop beats are internal bookkeeping and stock only. Listmonk needs an SMTP provider to send; the beat claims no delivery.
library-reading assumes the poet's audio file is already on the Core; AudioMass only edits audio. The reading evening in garden-lights is a family event at home.
Motif: the manuscript (cannot be made twice). Beats library-draft, library-newsletter, library-manuscripts, outro-street, closing.
